newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker in lackluster dealings.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker in lackluster dealings.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker after a fourth consecutive lightly-traded lackluster session, the market ending the week on a bearish note after the heavy liquidation by funds that came to a head on Monday, traders said.

There was some disappointment with the modest 325-tonne dip in stocks reported by the LME Friday following the draw of several thousand tonnes earlier in a week as the exchange introduced daily reporting of stocks on an experimental basis for six months.
LME stocks fell some 14,800 tonnes during the week to 159,675 tonnes.
May COMEX settled 1.30 cents weaker at 106.45 cents per pound, traded 107.40 to 105.60 cents. Spot April went out 1.05 cents lower at 107.85 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots compared to Thursday's 4,411 lots.
LME three-months needed to break above $2,300 and May COMEX above 108.00 cents to reverse the current weakening trend, Lawson Spence of Smith Barney said.
Bette Raptopoulos said copper was reflecting bearishness in many commodities and the stock market. "It's a shift to liquidity. I think it will resurrect itself soon," she added.

The market failed to react to Phelps Dodge Corp's reiteration this week that its offer of a pay freeze to workers at the Chino mine in New Mexico was final, Raptopoulos noted, adding that it was an issue the market should bear in mind.
The union and Phelps meet April 24-25 to discuss a new labor deal to replace the previous one which expired on June 30 last year.
Kennecott also confirmed its Utah smelter will close for 42 days starting sometime this month. Matte and refined metal output would continue for much of the shutdown.
